lines: There goes the first lamp! Then the next. Like a necklace!
Henri, the lamps! Count them with me. One, two, three...
Every lamp says bonsoir to the next one. So polite!
Lamps on! Now my knitting has its own little spotlight.
The lamp over our bench, last as always. Take your time, dear.
When I was a girl, a man lit them with a long pole. Now, pouf!
Lamps on, so it is officially evening. I make the rules.
Henri, your hat has a golden rim now. The lamp did that.
The lamps came on and the palms got their shadows back!
A moth at every lamp already. Little regulars, like us.
Each lamp a little pear of light. I could pick one.
Lamps on, and the sky still pink. Both at once! Greedy town.
Henri timed them once. Eleven seconds, end to end. Clever man.
Down it goes, into the bay. Like a peach into a bath!
The sea is wearing the sun as a brooch. Very chic.
Henri, quick, make a wish. The sun is dipping its toe in.
Forty-one years of sunsets on this bench. Not one the same!
Look at the gold path on the water, right up to our shoes.
Shh, everyone. The sun is sitting down. Let it get comfortable.
The whole bay has gone orange. Even the gulls look tanned!
Half a sun! Now a quarter. Now a little smile. Bravo!
Same seat tomorrow, sun? We will save it for you.
Henri takes his hat off for the sun. I find that gallant.
My grandmother called this the sea's supper. I always agreed.
That pink on the water! I want a scarf in exactly that.
The sun touched down and the whole railing said ooh. Me too!
One star, two stars. The sky is laying the table too.
Marcel, look up! Your string lights have competition.
The stars are out. My glass has one floating in it!
Henri says that one is a planet. I call it a star anyway.
First star of the evening. I wish for a second slice. Done!
Léo says the bright one is Venus. That boy knows everything!
Stars arriving like guests. Fashionably, one at a time.
So many stars tonight! Somebody has polished them.
Henri proposed under a sky like this. I said yes before he asked.
Stars over the sea, candles on the table. Spoilt, we are.
There's the little one that always twinkles. Hello, dear.
Henri, the stars! Put your glass down and look up.
The moon is up over the bay. Round as a cheese plate!
Henri, the moon has laid a silver path right to our table.
Bonsoir, moon. You look very rested tonight.
The moon in the bay and the moon in my glass. Two moons!
That moon could read a newspaper by itself. So bright!
The moon is following us home, Henri. Like Biscuit does.
The moon has put silver on every roof tile. Every single one!
A moon like a lantern. And nobody had to light it.
Waxing, says Henri. Smiling, say I. Both true.
Moonlight on the tablecloth! Marcel, save your candles.
A moon this round deserves a toast. To you, moon! Santé!
Ah, {name} is home! The window just went gold.
{name}'s light is on. Safely in, kettle on, I bet.
There's {name}'s window! I know it by the curtains.
{name} is home. I shall wave. They can't see. I don't mind!
Another window! {name}, this time. The town is filling up.
{name} is home in good time. Feet up, I hope.
A new window lit. {name}! I keep a little list in my head.
From our table I can see {name}'s window. Hello, little lamp!
Every window that lights up is somebody's good evening. {name}!
{name}'s window just went dark. Bonne nuit, {name}!
There goes {name}'s light. Sweet dreams up there.
{name} has gone to bed. Sensible! Henri, look, a sensible person!
Lights out for {name}. I shall whisper it: dors bien.
{name} is asleep already! We are the night owls, Henri.
Bonne nuit, {name}. The moon will keep your window company.
Twelve bells from the old town! Right on time for the tarte.
The bell says noon. Marcel says lunch. Both very wise.
Six o'clock from the old town. The evening officially begins!
Six bells. Henri always counts them under his breath.
We were married under that bell. It still rings for us, I think.
Hear it? The church up the hill. Like someone humming far off.
That bell has a little crack in its voice. I adore it.
The bell! Arm, Henri. We shall walk in time with it.
Every table taken! Marcel is doing a little ballet with that tray.
A full terrace! Four languages and one baby. I love it.
Henri, budge your chair. That family needs one more seat.
So many cups clinking! Like a wind chime made of saucers.
I know eleven people here. No, twelve! Bonjour, Camille!
The next table ordered the tarte because I said so. Ha!
The terrace sounds like a hive. A very polite hive.
Every parasol has a little party under it. Bonsoir, all!
Rosé on every table already! The evening has started early.
Every candle lit, every chair full. The café is glowing!
Such chatter tonight! I shall have to gossip louder.
Marcel has not sat down once tonight. I am saving him a smile.
The terrace is packed! Marcel will sleep like a log tonight.
The music! Henri, finish your glass. We are only watching. Mostly.
There is the accordion. The first tune is always the slow one.
Music and string lights together. Like a curtain going up!
Somebody has to dance first. Brave young things!
A waltz to start! Henri, that is practically an invitation.
Marcel turned the music up a notch. I saw that, Marcel!
Here it begins. I will narrate, Henri. You keep time.
Bravo! Somebody start the clapping. Me! I will start.
The accordion is warming up. Like a cat having a stretch.
Music already? Henri, up! Our chairs at the café are waiting.
Théo spun Camille twice! Did you see, Henri? Twice!
We danced like that once, Henri. Well, I danced. You trod.
The accordion player has his eyes shut. He knows it by heart.
A tango now! Somebody's grandmother is showing them how.
My shawl is swaying all by itself. It wants to join in.
Henri, your knee is doing the waltz under the table.
The string lights jiggle when they stamp. Even the bulbs dance!
The music floats right to our table. Front row, no ticket!
That tall young man dances like a heron. Very elegant!
We are walking home in three-quarter time, Henri. Listen!
That couple has danced every song. Married sixty years, I bet!
Look, their shadows are dancing on the café wall too!
Marcel just did a little twirl with his tray! I saw it!
That girl is dancing with her shoes in her hand. Very sensible!
A crowd at the railing! Everyone came for the same show.
Look at them all leaning, Henri. Like swallows on a wire.
Yusuf and Biscuit have the front row. Biscuit always does.
We don't need the railing. Our bench is a royal box.
That couple at the end is whispering. Sunsets keep secrets.
I know half that crowd by the backs of their heads!
Everyone went quiet at once. Like in church, Henri.
The crowd's shadows are as long as the whole promenade!
Somebody always says "ooh" at the last bit. Tonight, me!
Strangers at the railing, chatting like cousins. That is sunset.
Henri, let us walk behind the crowd. Pardon, pardon, merci!
Everyone at the railing wearing the same smile. Matching!
Bonjour, {name}! How lovely to see you out and about!
{name}! Come by for tea on Sunday. I mean it this time!
There goes {name}. Always on the sunny side of the street.
{name}, you look rested! Whatever it is, keep doing it.
Henri, wave! That was {name}. Oh, too late. Next time.
{name} waved with both hands. I shall wave with both back!
Ah, {name}! I was just telling Henri about you. Nice things!
{name} smelled of oranges just now. Somebody's been peeling!
Good morning, {name}! There's room on the bench, you know!
{name} is humming. I know that tune! It's on the tip of my tongue.
Henri, did {name} say bonjour or bonsoir? Both, I think.
{name}, a leaf in your hair! No, keep it. It suits you!
That was {name}. I knew those footsteps. Light as a waltz.
{name} is in a hurry. Someone nice is waiting, I hope!
Bon appétit, {name}! Marcel has the tarte today. Go on!
Lucie! The baguette is winning the race again!
There goes Lucie. The bread will be home before the butter.
Lucie has flowers in her basket. And a leek! Very chic.
Lucie waved and steered with one hand. Henri gasped. I clapped.
Our Lucie, round and round. She knows every cobble by name.
Lucie's scarf flew out behind her like a little flag. Bravo!
Lucie goes by and every gull looks up. Bread radar!
Errands again, Lucie? You do the whole town's shopping!
That girl could cycle to Paris and back by teatime.
Lucie! Save me a pain aux raisins tomorrow! She nodded. Deal!
Inès! Look at those legs go. I was like that once. Briefly!
Inès flew by. Henri, did you feel the breeze? That was her!
Allez, Inès! One more lap and then a lemonade!
Inès runs as if the sea had invited her somewhere.
Inès is racing the sunset again. I know who wins. Inès!
Inès's ponytail goes like a metronome. Tick, tock, tick!
I told Inès to enter a race. She says this IS the race.
Inès, darling, you'll overtake your own shadow one day!
Henri jogged once, in 1983. Inès still asks about it. Ha!
Biscuit! Bonsoir, little sir! Is Yusuf walking you, or you him?
Biscuit looked at my handbag. He remembers what's in there!
There goes Biscuit, very busy. Important sniffing to do.
Biscuit's ears go up when he sees Henri. Henri's too!
Yusuf has his lantern out. Biscuit is leading the parade!
Biscuit trots like he's late for a meeting with the mayor.
Henri, Biscuit winked at me. Don't laugh. He did.
Yusuf! Tell your mother the pistachio pastries were divine!
Biscuit's tail goes like a little windscreen wiper. Swish!
Léo! Walk, darling! Oh, he's gone. Run, then!
Léo is a little comet. Look, his sock is coming down.
Léo said bonjour backwards as he ran. Ruojnob! Clever boy.
Henri, remember running like that? No? Me neither. Ha!
Léo has jam on his cheek. Strawberry, I'd say.
That boy has two speeds: fast, and fast asleep.
Léo shouted 'Bonjour Madame Odile!' at full tilt. A gentleman!
Camille will be after him in a minute. There she is! Ha!
Léo ran by with a feather in his hand. Treasure, no doubt.
Asgeir! Hei! He taught me that. Hei, hei!
There goes Asgeir, thinking. You can see the ideas from here.
Asgeir walks like a Norwegian. Steady, as if it were snowing.
Asgeir, come and sit! He smiled. That means later.
Asgeir carries his baguette like a violin. So careful!
Asgeir waved at Henri. Henri waved his newspaper. Men!
Asgeir, a hat in this sun! Norwegians, honestly.
Asgeir was humming the builder's tune. It's catching!
There's Asgeir. I must ask him about the robots' letters.
Asgeir stops for this light every evening. Like a sunflower.
Ding! That's Lucie. Nobody else rings so politely.
Lucie's bell. Two rings is bonjour, one is mind out.
There's the bell. Ding-ding! Like a teaspoon on a cup.
Every time Lucie rings, Henri lifts his hat. Forty years of it.
I hear that bell and I think: bread! Every single time.
Ding! I rang back with my bracelets. She heard, I'm sure.
A bell behind us. Lucie, or an angel getting its wings!
Hark at that gull. He sounds like Henri finding his glasses.
A gull! Telling everybody the news. Like me!
That gull has opinions. I respect a gull with opinions.
Hush, Henri. The gull is singing. Well. Shouting nicely.
A gull! Bonjour, monsieur! He never answers. Proud bird.
Every gull call sounds like a laugh at a very good joke.
That gull is calling his wife. Henri, call me like that!
Listen! A gull over the water. Summer is still with us, then.
Gulls at lunchtime. They can smell Marcel's tarte, I'm sure.
A gull over the bay! Henri, put your crossword down and look.
Henri sets the pace. A snail would call it leisurely!
Henri is pointing his cane at the view. Showing it off!
Henri is pretending to think. He is waiting for me to say it.
Henri saved my side of the bench with his hat. Gallant!
Henri is stirring his coffee like it owes him a secret.
Henri has his glass raised already. To what, darling? To us!
Henri is folding his napkin into a swan. A sort of duck.
Marcel, three cups on one arm! Look, Henri, look!
Marcel is weaving between the chairs like a waltz.
Marcel just winked at table six. He winks at everyone. Good!
Marcel carries the rosé like it might be a christening.
Marcel, a pirouette with a full tray! Bravo, bravo!
Marcel brushed a crumb off a chair before anyone sat. Lovely.
Inès! Faster than the sun! It is losing, look!
There goes Inès, ponytail first. Allez, Inès!
Inès is on her second lap. I counted. I always count!
Inès is eating her lunch at a gallop. Chew, darling!
Inès at a café table, sitting still! Henri, write it down.
Inès is at the railing, catching her breath and the sun.
Inès with a glass of rosé. Even she has a slow lap.
Inès dances like she runs. Very quick feet!
Inès is walking and typing at once. Clever girl!
Yusuf is being walked again. Biscuit has the map.
Yusuf stops at every lamp post. Biscuit insists. Patience!
Yusuf and Biscuit at the railing. Two gentlemen at the opera.
Yusuf's lantern, bobbing along. Like a little firefly!
The night round! Yusuf, wrap up, it is breezy by the water.
Biscuit is sniffing the lavender. A dog of taste!
Biscuit is sitting for the sunset. Best manners in town.
Biscuit in the lantern light! His shadow is twice his size.
Biscuit is waiting for Yusuf to finish his call. So patient!
Lucie with her basket full! Errands on wheels.
Lucie took the corner like a swallow. Ding, ding!
Lucie is toasting the sea. The sea looks flattered.
Lucie and her rosé. She holds the glass like a tulip.
Lucie said she would not dance. Look at her now!
Léo is running round the fountain. That is lap nine, at least!
Léo is chasing his friend round the fountain. Or the other way!
Léo is counting the coins in the fountain. He knows them all.
Léo is lying on the fountain edge. Studying fish that are not there.
Léo with his citron pressé. Such a serious little face!
Léo is practising his dance moves. That one was a jump!
Léo is waving goodbye to the sun. The sun will be back, darling!
Léo is bargaining with his mother for five more minutes.
Camille is calling Léo from the fountain again. Good lungs!
Camille, a wave! I shall wave back twice.
Camille has the salade niçoise. She eats it so elegantly!
Camille stopped to sniff the jasmine. I saw! I do that too.
Camille at the railing, glowing like a painting. Lovely girl.
Camille is herding Léo homeward. The gentlest shepherd!
Camille has a glass and her feet up. Léo must be in bed!
Camille is dancing with her eyes closed. That is the good kind.
Théo is working from the column again. Very hard. Ha!
Théo is on the phone and watching the gulls. Both, darling!
Théo is explaining something with his fork. Very passionately.
Théo is strolling like a man with nowhere to be. Lucky man.
Théo is calling Camille over to the railing. Such a romantic!
Théo just clinked glasses with Camille. Every evening, like us.
Théo is dancing! He never promised, Camille says. Ha!
The builder is drawing boxes on a napkin. Little arrows too!
The builder is eating with one hand and thinking with the other.
The builder is taking his ten minutes at the railing. Good boy.
Asgeir is asking Henri about the lemons. Henri is beaming.
Asgeir has a baguette under his arm. Now he looks French!
Asgeir is walking with his hands behind his back. Thinking!
Asgeir is waving at everyone. I got a wave! Two, actually.
Henri has fallen asleep with the pencil in his hand. Sweet.
Henri is tipping his hat to Camille. And now to the lamp post.
Marcel is bringing olives to everyone. He sees me looking!
Marcel is carrying our tarte. Henri, sit up straight!
Marcel is still smiling at this hour. Where does he keep it?
Yusuf is talking to Biscuit like a colleague. Lovely.
Biscuit found a leaf and is carrying it like a newspaper.
Lucie rang her bell at me! Ding to you too, darling!
Lucie is laughing at the drinks table. I can hear it from here!
Léo is swinging his legs under the table. So far to the floor!
Camille is taking a photo of the sea. It always says yes.
Théo is deciding between rosé and pastis. It will be rosé.
Théo is leaning on the railing like a film star. Handsome!
The builder is watching the arcade sign. Like a proud uncle.
Asgeir stands by our bench like a page boy. Sit, darling!
Asgeir passed us on his walk. Same loop as us, but faster!
Somebody wished on a button. I can see it. Very hopeful!
Round the fountain, Henri. The long way. It is shorter.
The pigeons are bathing in turns. Such good manners!
Look, a coin landed heads up. Whoever threw it, lucky you!
The spray has made a tiny rainbow. Henri, quick, before it goes!
I threw a coin in here in nineteen eighty-four. Still waiting. Ha!
The water has turned gold. Every coin looks brand new.
A sparrow is drinking from the edge. One sip, look around, sip!
The stone fish in the middle has been spitting for a hundred years.
A leaf is going round and round the basin. Taking the tour!
Léo is winning! No, the other one is winning! No, Léo!
Round and round! I am dizzy just watching them, bless them.
Léo, your laces! Oh, he is gone again. Next lap, Léo!
Henri, you raced me round that fountain once. You let me win.
They are counting laps out loud. Twelve! Fourteen! Twelve again?
Not so close to the water, boys! Oh, too late. Wet sleeve!
Ten o'clock and Léo has already run a marathon. Round a fountain.
Again! Léo said again! Where do children keep all that run?
The pigeons have given up and moved to the café. Very wise.
Let them pass, Henri. They are on lap twenty and very serious.
Bravo, both of you! Everybody gets a medal from Odile!
The sea is so flat today you could iron a shirt on it.
Morning sea, all silver buttons. Henri, look how it sparkles!
Such a blue! Bluer than my good china, and that is very blue.
The water has little white lace edges today. Very elegant.
The sea is turning peach. In a minute, apricot. Then rosé!
The sea and sky are the same blue now. Where does one stop?
Listen. Hush, hush, hush. The sea is telling the stones a story.
I have looked at this sea for forty years. Still not bored. Ha!
The breeze off the water has salt in it. Good for the cheeks!
The gulls are sitting on the water like little bathers.
Henri, fold the paper. Our walk is calling.
Soon we walk. I shall take your arm and all the gossip.
A little stroll before the light goes gold. Up, darling!
My cardigan for the walk. Henri says July. I say just in case.
The crossword can wait. The promenade cannot. Arm, please!
Nearly at the bench. My feet have been looking forward to it.
A sit-down soon. I have saved the best news for the bench.
The evening bench, Henri! Front row for the colours.
Let us sit by the railing soon. The sky is warming up.
A few more steps, then we sit and watch the windows light.
I want our bench before the sun starts. Hurry, but slowly!
Henri, the second bench. The one that faces the sunset.
Lunch at Marcel's in a minute. I shall have the tarte. Again!
Henri, stand up slowly. Then straight to our table.
Soon coffee. I have been rehearsing my order all morning.
Marcel will have our table ready. He always does!
Two forks, one tarte. The plan for lunch is very simple.
Shall we go to Marcel's for a glass? Half a glass. Yes!
The café lights are on. Our little table is calling.
Soon a glass of rosé, Henri. To forty-one years again!
I shall wear my good scarf to the café. The evening deserves it.
Off to the terrace soon. I want to hear the music start.
One more look at the sky, then wine and gossip at Marcel's.
Home soon for a little lie-down. Then back for the crossword!
After lunch, a nap. Henri snores in waltz time.
Merci, Marcel! We go home now and dream of your tarte.
Home to water my geraniums. They will want to hear about lunch.
A siesta soon. The shutters half closed, like the whole town.
The young ones can have the dance floor. We have pillows.
Bonne nuit soon, everyone! I shall say it twice to be sure.
Henri, finish your glass. Our pillows are waiting!
Home to my slippers. They have been so patient all day.
A last wave to Marcel, then home to bed.
Soon the lamp off. I shall write today in my diary first.
Bedtime soon. I will lay out the blue dress for tomorrow.
Home, and a cup of warm milk. The perfect last chapter.
The post office sign just went bright! Somebody's robot wrote home!
Henri, the sign! An agent sent a letter. At this hour!
There, it flashed! I do hope it was a thank-you note.
Ooh, the post office winked at me. I winked back.
Henri, look. An email for a robot. Or from one. Both, perhaps!
That glow means a letter went out. Asgeir told me. I remember!
There goes another! Like a little lighthouse for letters.
A letter at lunchtime! The agents work right through the tarte.
Flash! I always say bon voyage to the letters. Bon voyage!
Henri, did you see? The post office blinked. Like Marcel winking.
An agent just answered an email. Prompter than Henri, bless him.
The sign brightened. I like to think it was a birthday card.
Half a glass, and the post office still at work. Santé, agents!
The post office glowed! Does the agent lick the stamp, Henri?
Three flashes since my tarte arrived. Busy little post office!
Ah, the sign! An email off into the evening. Off you go, dear.
The post office just brightened. Asgeir would be so pleased!
The sign again! Who writes letters at teatime? Agents do!
Good morning, post office! Busy already, I see!
The arcade lit up! Somebody just filled in all their blanks!
Ooh, the arcade sign! I hope they chose magnificent.
Someone finished a Fun Libs story! I hope a walrus was in it.
The arcade flashed. Henri, someone somewhere is giggling!
Bravo, whoever you are! The arcade says you finished.
A story just got its blanks! Noun or verb? Léo would know.
The workshop sign just glowed. A helper found its tool!
Toolrails lit up! Some robot borrowed a screwdriver, Henri.
The workshop lit up. Like the little bell on a shop door!
Bravo, little lamp! You were the first again.
Every lamp along the railing at once. Well, nearly once!
Look, the lamps have put little gold rings on the stones.
The lamps are on. That is my signal for the cardigan.
The lamps came on and the gulls went quiet. Manners!
Plop! Did you hear it, Henri? The sun just met the sea.
The sun is sitting on the water like a hen on her eggs.
Hold still, everyone. This is the best part. There!
Every evening it does this, and every evening I gasp.
The bay has gone pink right up to the railing. Ooh!
Going, going... I always clap when it is gone.
My cheeks are orange, Henri. So are yours! Look at us.
Two stars now. Three! They come out like shy children.
The first stars, and the first sip. Perfect timing.
Star light, star bright... Henri, what was the rest?
The stars are out early. They heard there was music.
My mother said each star is a lamp someone forgot. Sweet!
The moon over the bay always looks like it is listening.
The moon lights the whole promenade. The lamps can rest.
Henri, look, {name} is home. Right on time, as ever.
That light is {name}. I could set my watch by it.
Bonne nuit, {name}. The window has closed its eye.
{name} has gone to bed. Henri, they beat us again!
{name} is asleep. I will whisper from now on.
Twelve! The bell up the hill is ringing us to lunch.
Listen, the church! Twelve soft bongs from the old town.
Six o'clock bell. Arm, Henri, we have a sunset to catch.
Such a happy noise. Cups and spoons and gossip. Lovely!
The café is full to the brim. Marcel is flying!
The terrace is so full we are practically dining together.
Bonsoir, table four! Bonsoir, table five! Hello, everyone!
Music! Henri, the music has started. Shoulders, at least!
The accordion! Here come the first brave ones. Bravo!
The string lights, the music... Henri, one waltz? Later?
Look at them turn under the lights! Like spinning tops.
I am dancing in my chair. It counts. Henri says it counts.
Henri and I danced right there. Under the same bulbs, nearly!
So many heads at the railing. Henri, stand up, you'll see.
{name}, bonjour! You walk like someone with a good plan.
Bonsoir, {name}! The light is following you, did you know?
{name}, off home? Sleep well, and dream of tarte!
Henri, it was {name}! I waved first. That makes a hundred today.
Lucie! Errands! Look at her pedal, Henri. Like a sewing machine.
Three loaves in that basket today. Somebody is having guests!
Lucie, you dropped a smile! No, wait, you kept it. Good.
She ran past and said bonsoir without losing a step. Talent!
There goes Inès. I counted her laps once. I lost count, she didn't.
Biscuit! Trotting like a little general. Bonsoir, mon général!
Biscuit and the lantern! Good evening, gentlemen!
Yusuf, he looked at me! Biscuit looked right at me. An honour.
Biscuit stopped for my shoe, then remembered he had places to be.
Whoosh! That was Léo. I felt the breeze in my curls.
Léo waved while running. Nine and three quarters, and so polite!
There goes Léo with a stick. A sword today. Tomorrow, a wand.
Léo, slow down! No, don't. You're doing it beautifully.
Asgeir and a baguette! He's nibbled the end. I saw that!
Asgeir nodded at me like a gentleman. Henri, take notes.
There goes Asgeir, chasing the light. He'll catch it, that one.
The bell! Henri, look up, Lucie is waving at us.
A gull! Shouting at the sea. The sea doesn't mind at all.
Listen, Henri, the gull is gossiping. Probably about us!
That gull laughs at everything. A good audience.
A gull calling over the water, in that golden light. Opera!
Past the fountain, Henri. Splash my fingers, then on we go.
I'll be the referee, boys! Everyone wins! There.
Two boys and a fountain. The whole Olympics, right there.
The sea is wearing its morning blue. Henri's eyes, a bit.
The sea is blushing, Henri. All the way to the edge!
Inès with a glass! She has earned every drop of it.
Inès at the railing, still pink from running. And the sky too!
Inès eats lunch outside, always. A woman after my own heart.
Marcel weaves through the tables like a fish. A tray-fish!
Marcel has a pencil behind his ear. He never uses it. Memory!
Marcel with the rosé tray. Every glass a little sunset.
Henri on our bench, hat on his knee. Isn't he handsome?
Henri is saving my chair with his cane. A true knight!
Look at Henri strolling. Forty years and still the same lovely walk.
Yusuf and Biscuit at the railing. Two silhouettes, one tail.
Yusuf is showing his mum the sky. Wave, Henri, we're on camera!
Yusuf follows Biscuit so patiently. Like a good butler.
Lucie with her rosé. Obviously! She always says obviously.
Camille and Théo! Dancing! Henri, they remind me of somebody.
The builder eats lunch with us! I must ask him what he builds.
Biscuit's nose is working overtime. Every lamp post a letter!
exchanges: Henri, the lamps! Our cue to hold hands.
My hand was already there, ma chérie.
Is it in yet? I blinked!
Only the bottom, darling. Look quick.
Henri, is the moon full tonight?
Nearly. Like my glass. Marcel, please.
You wave. I shall nod. A team effort.
The bell and my stomach agree, Odile.
And so shall we. After the last sip.
Six. I counted with my feet.
Marcel, you are everywhere at once!
Only twice at once, Odile. Your tarte is coming.
One song. A slow one. Then I sit and admire.

Already up, ma chérie. Already up.

Time to go home soon, darling.

Done. The same wish as last year. It keeps coming true.
